findings.checklist_item: In D2, call out that migrating the canary onto push_tickets_branch changes its runtime behavior (adds write-lock/epoch-guard/stash-repair, drops the sleep backoff) and add an AC that the canary smoke/behavior test confirms this convergence is intended and does not manufacture new best-effort false alarms.
evidence: reconcile-bridge-canary.yml:229-246 is a bare push/fetch/merge/sleep loop — no write-lock, no compat.store_epoch_merge_target, no stash repair, and `sleep $(( (1 << attempt) + RANDOM % 3 ))` backoff
push.py:228-360 wraps merge in write_lock + check_no_rebase_in_progress + store_epoch_merge_target + _resolve_conflicted_pop, and re-pushes with no delay
D2 discusses deleting the loop and updating the decision block but not that the canary gains locking/epoch-guard behavior and loses its backoff
findings.finding: D2 collapses the canary loop onto the same core entrypoint but does not acknowledge that the canary loop's RUNTIME behavior changes: it currently has no write-lock, no store-epoch guard, no stash/merge/pop repair, and retains a sleep backoff plus 4c4f defect-2 (no final push), whereas push_tickets_branch adds all of those and removes the sleep.
scenarios: Canary now takes the tracker write-lock and can hit LockTimeout/RebaseGuard best-effort returns it never previously exercised
Canary loses its RANDOM-jitter backoff, changing its contention profile in the alerting path

findings.finding: Strict mode and the new commit+push entrypoint both delegate to push_tickets_branch, which early-returns when _push_mode() resolves to 'off' or 'async' (push.py:170-206) before reaching any D5-enumerated branch. In a client config with sync.push=off (or async), the reconciler's strict entrypoint would return normally without pushing the commit-back — silently losing the inbound events that D4 says exist nowhere else, reproducing the exact failure this ticket removes.
findings.location: D5 / AC 'Strict mode fails loud on EVERY silent best-effort return'
findings.suggested_fix: Have the new CI entrypoint set REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always (or a strict-only override) so it always takes the synchronous push path, and add the off/async returns to the D5 fail-loud enumeration for the strict-mode contract.
